theme: El pretérito — contar lo que pasó; los marcadores del tiempo; David y Goliat (1 Samuel 17)
storyThread: David y Goliat (1 Samuel 17): el valle, los dos ejércitos, el gigante que gritó, David el pastor, la honda y la piedra, la caída del gigante y la celebración del pueblo. L1 = el pretérito de los verbos -ar (él/ella): la columna de la narración. L2 = el pretérito -er/-ir y las personas de la narración (llegué / llegaste / llegó / llegaron). L3 = las palabras de la historia: el valle, el ejército, la armadura del gigante, el pastor y sus ovejas. L4 = el tiempo de la historia (ayer, entonces, luego, por fin) y la palabra del versículo (corazón).
grammarTargets: THE PAST IS NOW TAUGHT — this is A1's ONE pretérito wave and it discharges the standing present-only rule for authored lines. Only REGULAR preterite forms are bound: the -ar 3rd singular spine (habló, escuchó, lanzó, cayó, ganó, celebró, oró, gritó, entró, peleó), the -er/-ir set (respondió, salió, volvió, subió, bajó) and the llegar person paradigm (llegué, llegaste, llegó, llegaron)

the llegar paradigm sits in ONE wave (a1-u02 tener / a1-u03 ir / a1-u05 levantarse precedent) and its members NEVER share a hear-choose set (C5/U5-7 conservative) — the person is resolved by the WRITTEN subject in gap-fill (a1-u04 E6 precedent)

IRREGULAR PRETERITES ARE NOT BOUND AND NOT USED IN ANY AUTHORED LINE: fue, dijo, vio, vino, tuvo, hizo, dio, pudo, estuvo, hubo, trajo + stem-changing 3rd persons (pidió, durmió, murió, sintió) → A2-U1. Legacy exception recorded, not re-served: unit-01 already ships creó, vio, era as Génesis-1 story words

present vs preterite is carried by the ACCENT (oró vs ora): the unit creates exactly ONE new accent pair in the pool and it is never a shared hear-choose set — the contrast is tested in gap-fill with the written time marker (U7-2)
time markers of the past: ayer, entonces, luego, por fin (+ después and primero re-passed from a1-u05); the marker is the tile and the sentence carries the sequence
scripture is exempt from the tense rule (standing ruling) — and 1 Samuel 16:7 is present-tense anyway («mas Jehová mira el corazón»)
waveNotes: l1 (10) = the -ar narration spine, all new: the ten 3rd-singular preterites the story needs (habló/escuchó/lanzó/cayó/ganó/celebró/oró/gritó/entró/peleó). oró is the pack's ONE present/preterite accent partner (ora, a0-verbs) — documented, never a shared set (U7-2). l2 (9) = the -er/-ir preterites + the person paradigm: respondió/salió/volvió/subió new + bajó (-ar, bound with subió as the hill/valley pair, documented contrast) + llegué/llegaste/llegó/llegaron in ONE wave (paradigm precedent) with the paradigm members never sharing a hear-choose set. corrió was CUT at authoring to hold the pack at 34 new ids (the band's observed ceiling) — it stays say-text only. l3 (12) = the story's nouns: 11 new + piedra RE-PASSED (a0-u05, new:false — the story's weapon, byte-identical gloss). The armory set escudo/espada/lanza sits together on purpose (the giant's armor vs David's sling — documented contrast set) but lanza/lanzó never share a set (U7-11). l4 (7) = the time of the story + the verse's word: 4 new markers (ayer/entonces/luego/por fin) + 3 re-passes (después/primero from a1-u05, corazón from a1-u05 — the scripture teaches-word, U7-3). Largest wave = l3 at 12 — exactly AT the 12-per-page threshold (DEFECTS #18); no split required, split 6+6 if the renderer threshold is strictly-below-12. l1/l2 = 10, l4 = 7. Wave 5 = adaptive replay from progress.misses (unchanged convention).

qna.grammar: A1 register per THEOLOGY-guide §3.1: THE PAST IS NOW TAUGHT — pretérito of REGULAR verbs only (this is A1's one pretérito wave; the standing present-only rule is discharged for authored lines from here on). Present tense remains for nouns and markers. No subjunctive; affirmative familiar imperatives only (toca, señala). IRREGULAR PRETERITES ARE NOT USED IN ANY AUTHORED LINE: fue, dijo, vio, vino, tuvo, hizo, dio, pudo, estuvo, hubo, trajo, pidió, durmió, murió, sintió → A2-U1. Every say is one idea and the target word is repeated in caption + sign. Scripture is exempt from the tense rule (standing ruling) and 16:7 is present-tense anyway.
qna.csa: Owner plain-truth directive applied: nothing softened, nothing added. A giant defies the armies of Israel, the army is afraid (miedo is named), and a shepherd boy answers him and wins — the chapter's own serious elements are named as the text names them. Death is stated plainly and NOT dwelt on (cayó; no gore, no invented blow-by-blow), no dialogue is invented, and NO 1 Samuel 17 wording is reproduced: the pack quotes exactly ONE verse (16:7). David's courage is attributed to God, which is the verse's own point — Jehová looks at the heart, not at appearance or size — and it is never a measurement device: no system scores a learner's courage, faith or character (INT-1 holds; no doctrine-assent gate anywhere). The giant's defiance and the army's fear are never used as pressure on the learner (CSA-2).
